bug.title: Step 10 hard-fails honest persistent signals as tripwire_fail; rejections must be recorded and flagged, not fail the node
bug.symptoms: Since 3fa7336, evaluate_node sets fail_class "tripwire_fail" and poisons the subtree whenever any of the six probes rejects. On real data, the honest 20d volatility signal is rejected by five probes; the header gives the measurements. Four gate tests fail: - tests/e2e/test_live_campaign_end_to_end.py::test_every_node_row_has_metrics_or_a_fail_class - tests/e2e/test_live_campaign_end_to_end.py::test_the_ledger_holds_one_debit_per_node_at_the_oracles_charges_budget - tests/e2e/test_live_evaluation_end_to_end.py::test_each_childs_metrics_land_on_its_own_node_row - tests/e2e/test_live_evaluation_end_to_end.py::test_each_child_is_debited_once_under_the_oracles_own_charges_budget
bug.reproduction_steps: uv run --all-packages pytest -n 4 --dist loadfile: 4 failed, 1648 passed. Separately, run deploy/campaign/tripwire_fp_check.py on the real snapshot: 20d vol is rejected by five probes.
bug.expected: - run_tripwires is unchanged: the same probes, verdicts and figures. - evaluate_node no longer sets fail_class "tripwire_fail" and no longer poisons on a rejection. A node whose pipeline succeeded stays fail_class None/"ok" with its metrics. perturb_stability and the axis figures are still recorded as today. - Every probe's outcome is persisted per node in a table tripwire_verdict (node_id, probe, rejected INTEGER, figure REAL NULL, measured INTEGER, recorded_at; PRIMARY KEY (node_id, probe)), created if absent and refreshed on re-evaluation. This happens identically for null and real nodes. - NodeEvaluation gains tripwires_failed: tuple[str, ...], in fixed probe order. The node_evaluated event carries it as "tripwires_failed", a list that is empty when clean. - One WARNING log line is written per flagged node, naming the probes. - Module constant TRIPWIRES_GATE_DISCOVERY = False, documented with this spec's measurement as the reason. Setting it True restores the hard fail (tripwire_fail and poison) for a deployment that wants it, and test_tripwire_step.py covers both settings. - tests/leakage/test_leaking_signal_caught.py keeps M1's exit. The leaking signals are still rejected by all six probes (a) and by time-shuffle plus label-permute (b). It now asserts this through tripwires_failed and the tripwire_verdict rows rather than through fail_class. The honest momentum case still has no rejection. - The four gate tests above pass unchanged. The orchestrator member suite and the root tests/ suite pass.
bug.actual: Root cause: step 10 treats a time-shuffle-family rejection as proof of leakage, but on real data persistent honest signals trigger it. The live pipeline's structural window clipping makes agent-code leakage impossible, so a hard fail costs real discoveries for little protection.
bug.constraints: The tripwires member is unchanged No file outside the five listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/

bug.title: Promotion does not consult the tripwires, so a node flagged for possible leakage could be promoted without review
bug.symptoms: With bug 1, discovery-time tripwire rejections become advisory rows in tripwire_verdict, but promotion.record_decision (decision.py) reads none of them. The protection moves to promotion only if promotion enforces it.
bug.reproduction_steps: Write a tripwire_verdict row with rejected=1 for a node, pre-register it, then call promotion.record_decision for it. The decision is recorded.
bug.expected: - New promotion.tripwire_gate with rejects_tripwire_flagged(node_id, *, database_url) and a TripwireFlaggedError whose message opens with the code word "tripwire_flagged" and names each rejected probe and figure. - The gate reads tripwire_verdict by its restated table name, as promotion restates other members' spellings, and never imports the tripwires or orchestrator members. - It refuses when any probe rejected. - It also refuses when the node has no tripwire_verdict rows at all ("not probed", code word "tripwire_unmeasured"), since a node that was never probed cannot be promoted as clean. - A probe recorded as not measured (measured=0) is not a rejection. A node whose every probe is unmeasured is refused as tripwire_unmeasured. - record_decision calls the gate before writing, beside its existing pre-registration check. A refusal writes nothing. - An explicit operator override is supported: record_decision(..., acknowledge_tripwires="<reason text, at least 20 chars>") records the decision anyway. It persists the reason and the probe list in a promotion_tripwire_override table (node_id PRIMARY KEY, reason, probes, recorded_at), so a promotion past a flag is never silent. - test_tripwire_gate.py covers: - a flagged node is refused, and its message names the probes - a clean node passes - an unprobed node is refused as unmeasured - all-unmeasured is refused - the override records and passes; a short reason is refused - a refusal writes no decision row It passes under pytest-xdist. The promotion member suite passes.
bug.actual: Root cause: the promotion path has no tripwire check, because step 10 used to fail nodes directly.
bug.constraints: Existing promotion refusals and their order are unchanged; the tripwire gate is added after them No file outside the four listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
